dimension_justifications.soundness: The central claims are unusually carefully bounded and supported for the stated single-model scope. Sections 3–5 formalize ownership invariants, separate relational exactness from the independent FP32 attention oracle, exercise nine matched-control live faults, and distinguish logical storage, allocated pages, allocator counters, and unmeasured service capacity. The limitations on page 8 explicitly prevent these checks from being mistaken for a completeness proof, scheduler evaluation, or production-capacity result.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper is cleanly typeset, logically ordered, visually polished, and precise about claim boundaries. Figure 1, Tables 2–3, and the Results subsections give a coherent contract-to-evidence progression. However, undefined internal labels such as RR2 and W, the interleaving of three evidence cohorts, dense audit vocabulary, and very small labels in Figure 1 and Table 8 create localized but meaningful verification friction.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The executable, phase-aware ownership audit is useful and more rigorous than token-only equivalence checks, but the paper explicitly presents no new cache policy, kernel, scheduler, or capacity result. Its evidence comes from one model, runtime, hardware family, schedule, and geometry, and page 3 states that transfer to another runtime is not demonstrated. Following the calibration guidance, meticulous auditing alone does not establish a broad ICLR contribution.

paper_summary: FORKAUDIT proposes an executable audit contract for hybrid LLM inference state containing paged full-attention KV and recurrent GDN state. It evaluates a 2×2 factorial of full-copy versus shared-document KV and materialized versus borrowed-immutable GDN bases on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, checking token, full-logit, logical-KV, and GDN equality across fan-outs. It supplements relational checks with eight dense-FP32 attention-row oracles, nine live fault injections with matched controls, phase-aware storage witnesses, and explicitly separated memory denominators. The primary result is a bounded reference audit rather than a new serving mechanism.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest contribution is the phase-aware ownership contract and its unusually thorough reference validation: Figure 1 and Section 3 distinguish immutable prefix aliases from mutable post-transition request state; Sections 5.1–5.3 then connect that contract to exact trajectories, direct storage-range witnesses, an independent attention-row oracle, and nine live mutation tests.
strengths: The abstract and Introduction state the problem, contribution type, strongest results, and exclusions with exceptional precision; page 1 explicitly rules out kernel, scheduler, completeness, and production-capacity interpretations.
Section 3 and Figure 1 provide a coherent conceptual model linking the two ownership factors to setup, first transition, generation, and audit replay.
Section 4.4 and Tables 5–6 carefully separate memory estimands and prevent allocator deltas from being presented as NVML usage, service capacity, or throughput.
Figure 2 and Table 4 efficiently summarize three complementary forms of evidence: independent numerical checking, factorial exactness, and fault sensitivity.
Section 6 is exemplary in distinguishing established findings from omitted settings and stronger evidence needed for transfer.
The rendered PDF has consistent typography and margins, readable main-text tables, no clipping or overlapping content, and a clear nine-page main-paper boundary before references.
questions: What do RR2 and W stand for, and can the manuscript replace these internal run labels with descriptive cohort names?
What precise rule made the eight books and oracle rows held out, and what immutable record establishes that the 0.005 tolerance and mutant list were fixed before the evaluated run?
Which parts of the audit contract have been exercised unchanged on a second hybrid model or inference runtime, even in a smaller-scale test?

Could the authors provide a single cohort map listing the primary factorial, earlier capacity cohort, supporting timing control, and cross-backend negative gate, together with the claims each cohort is authorized to support?

issues.location: Section 2 and Table 1, page 3; Section 6, page 8, especially lines 414–431
issues.observed_evidence: The paper presents the executable audit contract as its primary contribution but validates it only on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with one runtime, H20 hardware family, page geometry, schedule, and GDN implementation. Page 3 explicitly says the evidence does not show transfer to another runtime.
issues.why_it_matters: Without a second instantiation, it is difficult to distinguish a reusable audit abstraction from a highly polished forensic validation of one implementation. This limits contribution and significance even though the reference case itself is rigorous.
issues.required_fix: Either demonstrate the unchanged core contract on an independent hybrid model or runtime, or extract a sharper implementation-independent interface specifying mandatory state transitions, witnesses, and failure semantics while narrowing any field-level evaluation-standard language accordingly.
issues.verification_test: A new reader should be able to map the same contract fields to a second implementation and see at least one complete clean run plus representative faults, or identify precisely which contract elements remain implementation-specific.
issues.evidence_needed: An independent second instantiation with ownership witnesses and fault tests, or equivalently strong portability evidence for the contract interface.

issues.location: Abstract, page 1; Sections 4.1–5.5, pages 4–8; Reproducibility Statement, page 9
issues.observed_evidence: RR2 appears in the abstract without expansion, the earlier capacity cohort is introduced later, and the Reproducibility Statement adds a W execution, a smoke cohort, and a bytecode-disabled follow-up. The reader must reconstruct which run supports which claim across several sections.
issues.why_it_matters: The internal run nomenclature and dispersed cohort descriptions obscure the evidence hierarchy and make otherwise careful provenance harder to follow.
issues.required_fix: Replace internal labels with descriptive names or define them on first use, and add one compact experiment/cohort table listing scope, fan-outs, workloads, purpose, replay status, and authorized claims.
issues.verification_test: For every numerical result in Sections 5 and Appendix D, an unfamiliar reader can identify its cohort and authorized claim from one table without tracing internal labels through the paper.
issues.evidence_needed: No new experiment is required; this is an organization and terminology revision.

issues.location: Abstract, page 1; Section 4.1, pages 4–5; Section 5.2, page 7
issues.observed_evidence: The manuscript calls the validation held out and the oracle rows, tolerance, and mutation campaign preregistered or pre-fixed, but it does not state the book/query selection rule, the temporal lock mechanism, or the relationship between the earlier 80-row diagnostic and the final eight rows in enough detail to assess selection independence from the PDF alone.
issues.why_it_matters: These terms imply protection against adaptive selection. Without a concise operational definition, readers cannot determine how strongly the design guards against threshold or row-selection bias.
issues.required_fix: State the selection rule and timing for books, queries, oracle rows, tolerance, and mutants, and point to the exact immutable receipt or manifest that predates execution.
issues.verification_test: The cited record should hash the selections and thresholds and have a verifiable creation point before the primary run; the final rows should be derivable from the stated rule without outcome-dependent choices.
issues.evidence_needed: A preregistration or frozen-manifest receipt and a concise description of the selection procedure.

issues.location: Figure 1, page 4; Figure 2, page 7; Table 8, page 13
issues.observed_evidence: Figure 1 contains several labels that are small at normal page size, Figure 2 devotes substantial space to categorical EXACT and intended-gate blocks, and Table 8 uses very small monospaced paths that require zooming.
issues.why_it_matters: The central architecture and artifact map should be effortless to read in a printed or single-page view; currently the most verification-oriented visuals are the least accessible elements.
issues.required_fix: Enlarge or split Figure 1, compress Figure 2's categorical panels or replace them with a compact matrix, and use short artifact identifiers in Table 8 with full paths moved to a supplement or footnote.
issues.verification_test: Render the paper at final size and in grayscale; all figure labels and artifact identifiers should be comfortably readable without zoom, and the ownership factors should remain distinguishable without relying on color.
issues.evidence_needed: No new scientific evidence is required; revised final-size visual assets are sufficient.

ethics_concerns: No material ethics concern is apparent. The paper evaluates systems behavior on existing PG-19 data, makes no human-subject or downstream safety claims, and includes an appropriately bounded ethics statement on page 9.
llm_usage_disclosure: This internal review was produced by an LLM-based reviewer using the supplied manuscript PDF, rubric, calibration document, and output schema; no external repository files or prior reviews were consulted.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A successful application of the same audit contract to a second hybrid model or independent serving runtime, including clean ownership witnesses and representative live faults.
A clearly time-locked selection manifest for held-out books, queries, oracle rows, tolerance, and mutant specifications.
A more independent recurrent-state or end-to-end numerical oracle that reduces the remaining common-mode blind spot beyond selected full-attention rows.
A concise cohort/evidence map and enlarged verification-oriented figures that make the already strong evidence substantially easier to audit.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: A mismatch between the manuscript's aggregate claims and the archived shards, sidecars, mutation receipts, or allocator records referenced in Table 8.
Evidence that the 0.005 tolerance, selected rows, or fault list was chosen after inspecting primary outcomes.
Failure to reproduce the dense-FP32 oracle or intended-gate mutation outcomes from the supplied artifacts.
Discovery that shared code or state outside the selected attention-row oracle can produce identical compared trajectories despite violating the stated ownership contract.
review_limitations: The review was restricted to the supplied PDF, rubric, calibration file, and schema; the referenced research bundle and machine-readable artifacts were not available for independent replay.
Citation metadata and support were assessed only from the manuscript's presentation and were not externally verified.
Visual assessment used rendered PDF pages, but no physical print test was performed.
